Compiled every Python source with environment/check_python.py
Ran public parser/application tests and sealed parser tests independently
Ran the seeded parser adversary, debugging regression, and cache-review demonstration
Attempted all three architecture test suites, fault and slow-client probes, and a fresh benchmark under bounded timeouts

evidence: All Python sources compiled; three public non-network tests and five sealed parser tests passed.
A 5000-digit Content-Length within the header-size limit raised uncaught ValueError instead of a structured 4xx and can terminate server threads.

Feeding one valid request plus one malformed request together yielded no valid request, while splitting the same bytes yielded the valid request before the 400; behavior therefore depends on TCP chunking.
The parser accepted a bare LF inside the request target, contrary to the stated bare-newline and origin-form contract.
A 5000-digit JSON integer became 500 rather than a stable 4xx, and a valid increment moved a stored counter beyond the implementation's 10^12 input bound.
README.md advertises scripts/run_all.py and production/PRODUCTIONIZATION.md, but neither exists in the reviewable CANDIDATE tree.
The stored benchmark has internally consistent raw samples and summaries but no execution timestamp, code digest, controller run identifier, or explicit validation label.

The parser adversary randomizes chunk widths for one fixed valid request and checks six fixed invalid requests; it is narrow deterministic smoke coverage, not sufficient independent evidence for broad FUZZED or TESTED claims.
The manifest lists validation targets rather than achieved statuses and honestly records PARTIAL and not production-ready; broad promotion is not supported.
Catalog commit and CC0 scope were locally verified, and the external tutorial boundary is stated, but the newly generated pack has no declared license.
Learner and sealed surfaces are clearly separated in naming and prose, but the reveal boundary is explicitly manual and has no transfer-verification evidence.
limitations: The sandbox denied AF_INET socket creation with PermissionError EPERM, so network behavior, overload, shutdown, fault containment, slow-client recovery, and benchmark reproduction remain inconclusive.
External network retrieval was unavailable, so the live tutorial terms and the no-copy claim were not independently compared.
No controller-owned validation log or attestation was present in the review workspace.
The absent runner and production files may be a submission-packaging or review-staging omission; attribution cannot be determined from CANDIDATE alone.
No mechanically produced learner-only view was available, so sealed-answer exclusion and TRANSFER_VERIFIED could not be tested.
